title: Bandgap References
intro: Every bias current, common-mode level and converter full scale on a chip is traced back to a reference: a DC voltage or current that should not move with the supply, the process or the temperature, or should move with temperature in a controlled way (Razavi, Chapter 12).

blocks.text: Reference design splits cleanly in two. First make the quantity independent of $V_{DD}$, which is done with self-biased loops whose current is set by a device and a resistor rather than by the supply. Then shape its temperature behaviour: proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT), constant transconductance, or temperature-independent. The last is obtained by adding a quantity that falls with temperature to one that rises with it, and bipolar junctions supply both: $V_{BE}$ falls by about 1.5 mV/K, and the difference of two $V_{BE}$s at unequal current densities rises as $V_T \ln n$.

Besides supply and temperature coefficients, a reference is judged by its output impedance (how well it holds still when the circuits it feeds kick it), its noise (which is added straight to whatever it biases or defines), its supply rejection at high frequency, and its power.

blocks.alt: Graph of voltage against temperature. A falling straight line is the base-emitter voltage VBE, a rising straight line is a PTAT voltage, and their sum is a nearly flat curve at about 1.2 volts.
blocks.caption: The whole idea in one picture: a falling $V_{BE}$ plus a scaled rising $V_T \ln n$ gives a flat sum near the silicon bandgap.

items: Supply-Independent Biasing: self-biased current loops, the $R_S$-defined current, supply sensitivity and start-up.
The Bandgap Principle: the temperature coefficients of $V_{BE}$ and $\Delta V_{BE}$, the op-amp core, and why the result sits near $E_g/q$.
Bandgap Design Issues: PTAT bias currents, CMOS pnp devices, op-amp offset, feedback polarity, curvature, output impedance and noise.
PTAT Currents and Constant-Gm Biasing: PTAT current generators, a current-based bandgap, and biasing for a temperature-stable $g_m$.
Low-Voltage Bandgaps: current-mode references below 1 V and a precision case study with supply regulation.

blocks.text: Typical numbers to remember: $V_{BE} \approx 0.7$ to $0.8$ V with $\partial V_{BE}/\partial T \approx -1.5$ mV/K at room temperature; $k/q \approx 0.0862$ mV/K; a zero-TC sum needs about $17.4\,V_T$ of PTAT voltage and lands near 1.2 V.

blocks.title: How flat is flat?
blocks.text: A reference reads 1.200 V at 27 °C and 1.203 V at both 0 °C and 85 °C (a parabola). Express its drift as an average temperature coefficient in ppm/°C over that range using the box method (total change divided by nominal value and range).
solution: The total excursion is 3 mV over 85 °C.
